title: Dengue serotype dynamics paper accepted at Lancet ID
text: The network’s flagship multi-country study on dengue serotype dynamics has been accepted for publication in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. This paper represents two years of collaborative data harmonisation across six MIDSEA member countries.

title: Response brief delivered to ASEAN health ministers
text: MIDSEA has delivered a policy response brief to the ASEAN health ministers’ meeting, presenting recommendations on cross-border disease surveillance informed by our model ensemble results. The brief covers dengue, malaria, and respiratory pathogens.

title: Open-sourcing the MIDSEA validation notebooks
text: We are releasing the MIDSEA validation notebook suite as open-source software. This collection of Jupyter and Quarto notebooks provides standardised checks for compartmental models, helping researchers verify that their implementations match published specifications.

title: MIDSEA 2026 — Bangkok
text: The flagship annual symposium of the MIDSEA network, bringing together researchers, public health practitioners, and policymakers from across South East Asia. Three days of plenary talks, thematic sessions, and hands-on workshops.

title: AMR surveillance methods · quarterly meetup
text: Quarterly meeting of the AMR working group to review progress on cross-country surveillance harmonisation, discuss new methods, and coordinate upcoming analyses.

title: Reproducible pipelines for vector models
text: A hands-on workshop on building reproducible analysis pipelines for vector-borne disease models. Covers containerisation, version control for model outputs, and automated reporting.

title: About
text:
MIDSEA is a network of early-career and senior researchers building transparent, regionally-grounded mathematical models of the infectious diseases that shape public health across South East Asia — from dengue and malaria to emerging zoonoses and AMR.
We connect modellers with public health agencies, share code and data, train the next generation, and coordinate rapid responses when outbreaks cross borders.

title: About
text:
Our principles



→ 01


Open, reproducible science
Every MIDSEA model ships with code, data provenance, and validation notebooks under open licences.

Practice



→ 02


Regionally grounded
Priorities set by the region: surveillance gaps, seasonal vectors, demographic realities unique to SEA.

Focus



→ 03


Training-first
Annual schools, short courses and paired mentorship turn modelling into a shared regional capacity.

Pipeline



→ 04


Policy-facing
Direct channels to ministries of health and ASEAN-level bodies so models land where they matter.

title: Bayesian inference for infectious disease
text: An intensive five-day summer school covering Bayesian inference methods applied to infectious disease modelling. Topics include MCMC, hierarchical models, prior elicitation, and posterior predictive checks.

title: Spatial epidemiology with R & Stan
text: A four-day short course on spatial epidemiology methods using R and Stan. Covers point processes, INLA, disease mapping on coarse surveillance data, and practical applications in South East Asian settings.

title: Join MIDSEA
text:
Membership is free and open to anyone based in or working on South East Asia — from first-year PhD students to senior professors, and from within and beyond academia.
What you get

Directory listing — profile in the members directory with a link to your work.
Annual symposium — reduced registration and travel bursaries for ECRs.
Slack & working groups — disease-specific channels, shared pipelines, quick code reviews.
Training access — free seats in every MIDSEA summer school and short course.

title: Call for Bangkok 2026 session chairs
text: We are now accepting proposals for session chairs at the MIDSEA 2026 symposium in Bangkok. The symposium will feature six thematic tracks, and we particularly encourage applications from early-career researchers. Proposals are due by 15 May 2026.

title: Meet the 2026 mentorship cohort — 24 new pairs
text: We are excited to announce our largest mentorship cohort to date: 24 mentor-mentee pairs spanning nine countries and six disease areas. The 2026 cohort includes researchers working on dengue, malaria, AMR, TB, respiratory infections, and zoonoses.

title: MIDSEA receives Funding Award extension
text: We are pleased to announce that the MIDSEA network has received a three-year funding extension to continue building the regional modelling hub. The extended grant includes capacity-building grants for four new partner institutions across the region.
